title: Panic over Kimberly Guilfoyle's outrageous Champagne demand and mystery righthand man
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Panic over Kimberly Guilfoyle's outrageous Champagne demand... but she digs in heels as Greek life unravels: 'I need him'

President Donald Trump picked Guilfoyle as ambassador to Greece in December 2024. At the time, sources warned her to be on her best behavior.

Actual Article Body:
By ELINA SHIRAZI, US SENIOR POLITICAL REPORTER

Published:  06:22 AEST, 2 October 2026   |  Updated:  08:09 AEST, 2 October 2026

Kimberly Guilfoyle has refused to cut loose an energy lobbyist who sits in on her meetings as US ambassador to Greece, the Daily Mail can exclusively reveal.

The 57-year-old former Fox News host, once engaged to Donald Trump Jr, has brushed off concerns over conflicts of interest.

'I need him,' she has said, half a dozen insiders told the Daily Mail.

But sources in Athens say the ethical concerns do not stop at Christos Marafatsos, 39, whose presence at Guilfoyle's official meetings was first revealed by the Wall Street Journal last week.

Her team has pressed a Greek hospitality fixer for freebies including two cases of Champagne and a nearly €1,600 ($1,800) dinner, three insiders told the Daily Mail. An embassy official said Guilfoyle paid for the meal.

At least two Greek outlets published, then quickly pulled, stories picking up the Journal's report as it made waves in Washington.

'Her team has forged excellent relationships with all the Greek media. They will call them up, and poof, there goes the bad press. Many people are afraid of getting on their bad side,' a Greek media insider said.

The storm has irritated Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who flies into Athens within days for talks with the Greek government, sources said.

'Rubio is annoyed but quite frankly has too much on his plate to worry about the side quests of Kimberly Guilfoyle,' a State Department source said.

'Rubio is annoyed but quite frankly has too much on his plate to worry about the side quests of Kimberly Guilfoyle,' a State Department source said

Christos Marafatsos and Kimberly Guilfoyle. Source: Christos Marafatsos/Facebook

President Donald Trump picked Guilfoyle as ambassador to Greece in December 2024, days after Don Jr was pictured out with Palm Beach socialite, and his now wife, Bettina Anderson. The Senate confirmed Guilfoyle last September.

At the time, sources warned the 'Margarita Girl' to be on her best behavior, cautioning that a posting in the land of Aegean islands and endless summers was not a license to party.

Guilfoyle was pictured in July sipping fizz and picking at grapes at Nammos, the jet-set hangout on Mykonos's Psarou Beach, alongside Bill White, Trump's openly gay ambassador to Belgium. She flew to Paris for Fashion Week the next day.

That month, Trump flew straight home from the NATO summit in Turkey without stopping in Greece, despite Guilfoyle promising locals a presidential visit.

The Guilfoyle scandal deepened on Thursday as top Democrats on the Senate and House foreign affairs committees urged Rubio to investigate her conduct, citing the Journal's report.

'If these reports are accurate, Ambassador Guilfoyle is unfit to represent the United States abroad and should be removed from her position,' Representative Gregory Meeks of New York, the top House Foreign Affairs Democrat, wrote to Rubio.

An embassy official said Guilfoyle 'continues to follow all State Department ethical guidelines.'

Marafatsos is a registered lobbyist for Aktor Group, a major Greek infrastructure and construction conglomerate that has expanded into natural gas distribution and renewable energy.

Guilfoyle has 'worked with companies across the energy sector' and has not focused on just one, her lawyer Jesse Binnall told the Journal.

Aktor paid Marafatsos $160,000 through June to build ties with the White House and the State and Energy departments, and Guilfoyle urged Balkan officials to do business with the company, the Journal reported.

Lawyers for Aktor told the Journal that the company's involvement began before it had any contact with the ambassador.

Marafatsos has worked closely with Guilfoyle in a non-governmental capacity, bridging the gap between Athens and the Greek-American diaspora, a source familiar with their working arrangement said. He also chairs Greeks for Trump, founded in 2016.
